items.name: flight_en
items.direction: Narrate this as a popular geography YouTube Shorts channel. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller: brisk and curious, natural emphasis, a short comic pause before each punchline, a hint of wonder on the route and the sunrises. Keep a lively, continuous pace (about 170 words a minute) with no long gaps; this is a 40-second Short. The first two lines are the hook: punchy and intriguing, stress 'west' and then 'east'. Stress the numbers. The last story line is a dry, quotable punchline. The final 'This is Bhoogol.' is a short, warm sign-off.
lines: From Australia, you fly west to reach Europe.
This plane flew east. Twenty-four hours, non-stop, and set the airliner world record.
The short way, past India, is about seventeen thousand kilometres.
But this jet crossed the Pacific, America and the Atlantic. Two sunsets, two sunrises, zero landings.
So why take the long way?
Because records count distance, not direction. Twenty-three thousand, one hundred and fifty-five kilometres. More than halfway round the planet.
The record it broke? A Boeing, in two thousand and five. It went the long way too.
Controllers even offered it shortcuts. The pilots said no.
Because in record books, the wrong way is the right way.
